items.title: Peel Highways Brace for 32 Scheduled Closures on Aug. 11
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the province has scheduled 32 separate closures across provincial highways in Peel Region for August 11, 2026. The affected routes include Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9 and the Queen Elizabeth Way, the same corridors that carry most commuter and commercial traffic through Mississauga and the surrounding region. Mississauga.com advises drivers to plan their route before heading out given how many highways are affected at once. The outlet's listing does not spell out a reason for this particular round of closures, though its coverage of other recent days has tied similar work to short-term repairs and routine highway maintenance. Anyone driving through Peel this week should build extra time into their trip and watch for detours. Mississauga.com also points readers to a separate closure list for anyone travelling to highways outside Peel Region.

items.title: Mississauga Shelter Manager Says He Would Rather Eat the Cost Than Keep Animals Caged
items.summary: According to NOW Toronto, Mississauga Animal Services has cut its pet adoption fee from $280 to $25 through August 22 as the shelter works to clear overcrowded kennels. Greg Madeley, the shelter's manager of animal care and wellbeing, told NOW Toronto the promotion was launched because there simply isn't enough space to keep taking in strays without risking overcrowding. He said watching the same pets live in kennels for years has weighed on him, and he's hoping the discount finally gets them into permanent homes. Madeley said the shelter will absorb the financial loss so the animals can live in a proper home instead of a kennel. Every animal available through the promotion has already been spayed or neutered, microchipped and vaccinated. NOW Toronto reports that in the promotion's first weekend alone, five of the shelter's 22 available dogs were adopted, with several cats finding homes as well. The shelter is also offering a foster-to-adopt option, letting people care for an unwell animal while the shelter covers its medical costs, with the option to adopt permanently if they fall in love with it.

items.title: Police Urged Him to Turn Himself In. A Day Later, This Brampton Man Was in Custody
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police have charged a Brampton man with aggravated assault after a stabbing at a commercial unit near Dixie Road and Aimco Boulevard in Mississauga on Aug. 1. Police say one adult male was stabbed and rushed to a local trauma centre in serious but stable condition, and is expected to recover. Investigators identified the suspect as 32-year-old Gregory Darling of Brampton and publicly urged him to turn himself in. INsauga reports Darling was arrested the following day, Aug. 2, and charged with one count of aggravated assault. He was held for a bail hearing and appeared at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton. Police are asking anyone with information about the incident to call Peel Regional Police at 905-453-3311, or to contact Crime Stoppers anonymously for a possible $2,000 reward.

items.title: A Mississauga Condo Resold at a $170,000 Loss Made Zoocasa's List of July's Cheapest Sales
items.summary: According to INsauga, citing data from real estate platform Zoocasa, home sales and prices across the Greater Toronto Area both slid in July, and Mississauga's five least expensive sales that month all went for under $400,000. INsauga reports the number of home sales in Mississauga fell 8 per cent month-over-month to 500 transactions in July. One example on Zoocasa's list was a one-bedroom-plus-den condo in City Centre with two full bathrooms, French doors on the den, a new dishwasher and a balcony view of the Toronto skyline. That unit sold for $380,000, well above its $299,000 asking price, even though the seller had paid $550,000 for the same property back in April 2021. The wide gap between that purchase price and its resale value reflects the kind of cooling Zoocasa's broader July figures point to across the city.

items.title: SIU Clears Officer After Struggle Ends With Man Tasered Outside a Motel Room
items.summary: According to INsauga, Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has cleared a Peel Regional Police officer of criminal wrongdoing after a man suffered serious injuries when he was tasered outside a Mississauga motel in April. The SIU said in a report released Monday that an officer encountered a man believed to be impaired, lying in the driver's seat of a Jeep parked with its lights on in a motel parking lot on April 25. The officer knocked on the window, and the man was initially unresponsive before slowly waking up and sitting up, according to the report. When the officer said he only wanted to make sure the man was okay, the man insisted he was fine and walked toward the motel's front doors, ignoring the officer's requests to stop, the SIU said. The man then became combative and punched the officer in the head before fleeing into the lobby of Hotel 6, at which point the officer used a taser on him. INsauga reports several other officers arrived to help, and the man was ultimately handcuffed. The SIU concluded there were no grounds for criminal charges against the officer.

items.title: Fake Eventbrite Listings Trade on Mississauga's Name for a Leadership Conference
items.summary: According to INsauga, the City of Mississauga is warning residents after discovering two Eventbrite listings that falsely claim to be affiliated with the city. INsauga reports the listings are for the International Conference on Leadership, Innovation, Global Investment and Professional Development, and claim the event will take place at Malton Community Centre on two separate dates, Aug. 31 to Sept. 2 and Nov. 30. The city said in a press release that it has no partnership with these events and that no booking exists for them at any city facility. Officials are urging residents and businesses to verify event details directly before registering or purchasing tickets. INsauga notes one of the two listings had already been removed from Eventbrite as of Monday, though the other remained live at the time of the report.

items.title: A Wrong-Way Turn on the QEW Turns Fatal for an 83-Year-Old Hanover Woman
items.summary: According to Ontario Provincial Police, an 83-year-old woman from Hanover has died after she drove the wrong way into oncoming traffic on the Queen Elizabeth Way in Mississauga. Mississauga.com reports the crash happened near Erin Mills Parkway on the night of Aug. 7, when the woman's sedan, travelling toward Toronto in the Fort Erie-bound lanes, collided head-on with another vehicle. Police at the scene initially believed both drivers had suffered only minor injuries. According to OPP, the wrong-way driver's injuries were later upgraded to life-threatening, and she died in hospital. Mississauga.com reports the crash remains under investigation. OPP is asking anyone with information or video footage of the incident to call 1-888-310-1122.

items.title: How a New Rapid-Assessment Clinic Diagnosed a Mississauga Mom's Skin Cancer in Two Weeks After Others Missed It
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Mississauga mother of three Liliya Leheta had her skin cancer symptoms dismissed by dermatologists for nearly two years before a new rapid assessment clinic at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre diagnosed her within two weeks of her referral. The Star reports Leheta first noticed her skin peeling on her chest in March 2023 after a day out with her kids without sunscreen, and later found a small red mole near the centre of her chest that she initially dismissed. Over the following two years, she watched the mole swell, change shape and bleed, all while an earlier referral to a specialist had been declined. In the fall of 2025, Leheta learned about the newly opened rapid assessment centre for skin cancer at Princess Margaret and was seen within two weeks of being referred there. She was diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma, the most common form of skin cancer in Canada, and a surgeon successfully removed the cancerous tissue less than two months later. The Star reports Leheta remains cancer-free today.
